quotes.text: Copilot for fabric is an AI assistant built right into Microsoft fabric. You type what you need in plain English, and it writes the code, builds the queries, or creates the reports for you.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Compact definition of what Copilot in Fabric does.

quotes.text: Copilot only works with data you already have access to. It respects your existing permissions. If you can't see a table in the warehouse, Copilot can't see it either.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies that Copilot does not bypass security controls.

quotes.text: If your data is messy, if tables aren't named clearly, if relationships aren't defined, copilot struggles. Garbage in garbage out still applies.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows why a clean data foundation decides Copilot's usefulness.

quotes.text: Copilot is a tool that accelerates learning, not a replacement for understanding. You still need to know what a join is, what a measure does, what a filter means.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable framing of AI assistance versus real skills.

quotes.text: This isn't about distrust, it's about ownership. If a report shows the wrong number, the business doesn't care that copilot wrote the measure. They care that you signed off on it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why every Copilot output must be reviewed.

chapters.title: What Copilot for Fabric actually is
What you need to use it

takeaways: Copilot in Microsoft Fabric is a data-focused AI assistant, distinct from Microsoft 365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot, that turns plain English into SQL, DAX, PySpark, pipelines and Power BI reports.
It needs a paid Fabric capacity and an admin-enabled tenant setting, costs nothing extra, and only works with data you already have permission to see.
Treat every output as a first draft: clean, well-modeled data and human review remain essential, while Copilot frees IT pros for architecture and tuning.
hook: Not every Copilot is the same. This episode explains Copilot for Microsoft Fabric in plain English for data beginners, analysts and IT pros, showing where it works across Data Factory, notebooks, the warehouse and Power BI, what you need to turn it on, and why human review still matters.
